examples.name: A new user can sign in and register for multi-factor authentication.
examples.methodology: This example does not run. If promoted, the browser and application flow would be real: the test would create a new account through the user interface, enroll an authenticator second factor, sign out, and sign back in with the password plus a current authenticator code before observing the account page. The identity backend would need an isolated test tenant or emulator, the authenticator-code helper would be test-only, and authentication responses would not be mocked. SMS and email enrollment are not covered.

examples.name: Signing in with a wrong password shows an error and does not open the account.
examples.methodology: This example does not run. If promoted, it would use the real browser and application flow with an isolated test account to submit a known wrong password, observe the visible error, verify that account navigation and multi-factor enrollment do not appear, then visit the protected account URL directly and observe the sign-in page instead of account content. The account credentials would be test-only, and authentication responses would not be mocked. This checks browser-observable access and does not inspect the identity provider's internal session storage.

examples.name: Water depth in meters equals the surveyed water elevation minus the surveyed bed elevation.
examples.methodology: This example does not run. If promoted, it would call the real production water-depth calculation through an imported production seam and compare exact known surveyed values: 103.75 m water minus 101.25 m bed equals 2.5 m, and 99.5 m water minus 100 m bed equals -0.5 m. Inputs are fixed test values; no calculation or response is mocked. It does not read a map or network response.

tests.name: Open the page on water for the Jalama Near Lompoc gauge Creek Segment only, with the camera framed there and no leftover synthetic ribbons.
tests.methodology: Opens the locally served page and waits until the read-only test seam reports ready. The browser page, ArcGIS SceneView, and committed published creek data are real. USGS imagery and USGS 3DEP terrain tiles are live external services; if they are unavailable the result is inconclusive rather than passed. Nothing is mocked or saved. The test-only seam supplies the water-segment list, water-graphic identity, and camera target. The test checks that only Creek Segment 27714637-026 has water, that exactly one water graphic exists for that segment, that the camera target is within 300 m of that segment's midpoint from the committed path, and that the removed synthetic controls are absent. It does not check the visual appearance of the water.

tests.name: Scrub to a different observation time and replace the shown water without leaving the previous water in place.
tests.methodology: Starts from the opening observation, then sets the real time slider to the published 2026-01-03T15:15Z flood peak and checks that the selected time and water-bucket identity change while exactly one water graphic remains on Creek Segment 27714637-026. The browser page and committed published data are real. USGS imagery and USGS 3DEP terrain tiles are live; if they are unavailable the result is inconclusive rather than passed. Nothing is mocked or saved. It does not check the visual appearance of the water.

tests.name: Play the Jalama gauge observations in chronological order, and stop that advance when Pause is pressed.
tests.methodology: Scrubs the real time slider to a mid-record observation taken from the committed series, presses the Play button, and samples the selected time until the samples have moved forward by 15-minute steps, then presses Pause and checks that the time stays unchanged for 1 second. The browser page and committed published data are real. USGS imagery and USGS 3DEP terrain tiles are live; if they are unavailable the result is inconclusive rather than passed. Nothing is mocked or saved. It does not check the visual appearance of the water.

tests.name: Select a Jalama gauge time with no observation and show no water on its Creek Segment.
tests.methodology: Selects a gap slot inside the committed series' 135-minute gap on 2026-06-09 and a null-reading slot from that same series, using the real time slider. It checks that the water-segment list is empty and that the status "No observation at this time" is visible in both cases. The browser page and committed published data are real. USGS imagery and USGS 3DEP terrain tiles are live; if they are unavailable the result is inconclusive rather than passed. Nothing is mocked or saved. It does not check the visual appearance of the water.

tests.name: Hide every numeric water-surface elevation, stage, and discharge value on the page.
tests.methodology: At the opening time, the published flood peak, and a gap slot, reads document.body.innerText plus every aria-label, aria-valuetext, and title value and checks that none contain a water number, the words stage or discharge, or the published water-surface elevations for those times rounded to 1, 2, or 3 decimals. The browser page and committed published data are real. USGS imagery and USGS 3DEP terrain tiles are live; if they are unavailable the result is inconclusive rather than passed. Nothing is mocked or saved. Console output and the visual appearance of the water are not checked.

tests.name: The catalog rejects a test entry that breaks the classification rules, and feature filters return each matching test once.
tests.methodology: Builds a sample catalog in memory, breaks one classification rule at a time, and checks that validation names that break, including a malformed catalog test identifier and a category prefix that does not match its category. It also checks that a feature filter returns each matching sample once. It does not open the catalog page, require the live catalog to contain zero tests, or run an application test.

tests.name: The release check runs the core tests first and stops before feature tests if a core test fails.
tests.methodology: Calls the same release-gate function the release command uses, with stand-in results. It checks that core runs first and that a failing or inconclusive core result stops the feature phase. It does not run the application or a real failing core test.
